utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: The first suspect in the line-up I created was Isak Musliu, also known as Qerqiz.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry interrupt. I wonder if Mr. Nicholls would be good enough to elicit the name of the officer who created the photo line-up on the computer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That could be done in cross, but of course I'll -- that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the officer who you tasked to create the photo line-ups?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I remember his first name. I know that he was an American, and I cannot for the life of me remember his last name. His first name was Barry. I believe he was from Texas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, did you in any way label or identify the photo line-up for Isak Musliu that you had had created?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: How did you do that what did you use?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I used U-1 concerning Mr. Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who was the suspect in the second photo line-up that you created?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: The suspect was Fatmir Limaj, also known as Celiku. And I labelled him U-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: As the investigation progressed, did you create other photo line-ups of other suspects?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: In this particular case?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you tell me where you obtain the photographs for the photo line-ups?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: CCIU had a database which at that time had access also to the KPS database or other pictures that were scanned and entered into the database. So the -- also from newspapers that people -- people had taken pictures and scanned them and built this database. So at that time we had a entered -- we had taken the pictures from the database.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And using that method did you have any difficulty obtaining photos to create the line-ups?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Sometimes there was difficulty. For example, if the suspect was wearing a beret, we had to find five more pictures of people wearing berets so we could keep the integrity of the photo line-up consistent. But in each case we always tried to find the same characteristic. If the suspect was wearing glasses, then five people would be added wearing glasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, for U-1, the photo line-up for Isak Musliu, and U-2, the photo line-up for Fatmir Limaj, how many different photo line-up versions were created, how many sheets?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I believe at least two.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are you sure of the number?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: No. It was possible that we even created three or four, but I believe at least two for each one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, can you describe - and you started to - from your training and experience the proper way to create photo line-ups? Not just specific to this case but the way photo line-ups should be created.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes. You almost want to try and keep the same characteristics consistent in the photo line-up. For example, if the suspect has a goatee, make sure that the other five people that you're going to enter in the photo line-up have goatees. You don't want to make one picture coloured of the suspect and have the other five pictures black and white. The photo line-up must be consistent with characteristics very similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You said the one photo of the suspect and the other five. How many -- how many photographs do you use when you create a photo line-up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: A total of six including the suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was that done with U-1 and U-2?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I asked you about versions of the suspects -- versions of the photo line-ups. Could you tell us about the order of pictures in photo line-ups, how they should be ordered or placed.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's my fault. You've created several versions, you said, or at least two versions of each photo line-up. I'm asking you about the order of the photographs and the placement of the suspect in different versions of the same photo line-up.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes. I never wanted to keep the suspect in the same number, so what I would do is I created a line-up that if he was -- he could be number 2 or maybe he could be number 4. The reason why I did this was to ensure that other witnesses were not telling each other, Hey, pick number 4 or pick number 2. So that way I always kept the line-up as fair as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And talking about the other five pictures that you would use in addition to the picture of the suspect, in different versions of the line-up, U-1 or U-2, would all those five pictures be the same or different; in other words, the same photographs used on all versions?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I would use the same photographs. I would just switch their Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you follow these procedures you've outlined in creating U-1 and U-2?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness P103 which is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, I have a redacted copy of that so it can be displayed. It's the same as P103. It just has the signature removed. That's behind tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you look at that series of photographs, sir. You can look at it to your left if that makes it easier for you rather than on the screen. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: This is U-1, suspect Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you -- is this the U-1 you've been talking about that you had created for you in this case?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I don't think I need to exhibit this redacted version, Your Honour. I just ask the record to reflect that P103 is the photo line-up for Isak Musliu, U-1, which the witness created.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at P104 now, sir, and that's under tab 2 in the booklet you've been provided. You can look at it to your left which may be easier. Same question: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: This is the photo line-up concerning Fatmir Limaj and which I had created.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And which -- just for the record, which number was assigned to this photo line-up?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Number 1 -- oh, I'm sorry. The suspect, you mean, or the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: This is U-2, suspect being number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again I'd just ask the record to reflect that the witness has stated he created this photo line-up sheet which is in P104.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to now look at a document which has not yet been exhibited. This is 0323-1631. That's at the last -- that's the last page of the booklet. I think the photocopy on the ELMO that we have may be missing the last digit from the ERN number, but this is 1631. Take a moment and look at this document if you can, please, sir. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was this?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: This is U-1, suspect Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you create this photo line-up sheet as well?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes. This is one that I had created.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you tell me if the same photographs are used -- well, that's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd ask to admit this, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be, Your Honour, Prosecution Exhibit P175.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll ask you, Witness, Mr. Kereakes, now, please explain to us the proper way, according to your training and experience, to present a photo line-up sheet to a witness, what steps you go through when you're asking them to look at a photo line-up sheet. Not specifically at this point to U-1 and U-2, but in general your understanding of the correct way to show a witness a line-up sheet.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I would bring in the witness or the victim into an interview room, at which time I had already placed the suspect photo line-up on a table. I which then would direct the witness/victim to take his time, look at each picture and see if this was one of the suspects in the case, at which time I would give them time, and he would look. I would then ask him if that indeed he did identify anyone to please circle the number and to sign it, at which then I took that suspect photo line-up and inventoried it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what about conversation during the process of the witness looking at the pictures?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I would not make any comments or engage in any type of conversation with -- with the witness/victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you follow those procedures you've outlined when you showed the photo sheets U-1 and U-2 to witnesses?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, what if a witness doesn't recognise anybody in a photo line-up? What do you do then?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And would that fact be noted anywhere in your reports or statements?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, it would. I would put in there that the victim/witness was not able to identify any suspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you remember the number or the approximate number of the witnesses that you showed U-1 to, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately -- no, three. Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what about U-2?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: U-2 was shown, I believe, to three also. I'm sorry, strike that. It was shown to two, two of my witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If the witness has identified somebody, circled a number and signed the photo line-up sheet, what then happens to the photo line-up sheet?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I then would attach it to his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you do that with U-1 and U-2 when you showed it to witnesses?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you about some specific instances in which you showed U-1 or U-2. Again, please remember not to use the names of these witnesses when we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you please describe the procedures you followed when you showed U-1 to this witness, and remember not to mention the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I took him in the interview room. I already had the suspect photo line-up on the table, at which time I told him again, "Take your time, look at each picture, look at each face, and tell me if you can identify anyone in this photo line-up." At which time I would remain quiet, and the victim then identified the suspect in this case, Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did you have the witness do when he identified Mr. Musliu?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I had him circle the number of the suspect, and also I had him sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember anything else that the witness said when he identified Mr. Musliu?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, would it help you to look at your notes of this interview?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you could look again at tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt. At the moment, as I understand the evidence, this witness has merely said, "I recognise these notes." He has not identified them as his, and before my learned friend goes any further, I'd invite him to do so, and in doing so, respectfully draw the Tribunal's attention to the fact that there is a signature at the bottom of these notes but not of this witness. So I wonder if my friend could please lay the foundation as to the provenance of these notes before he leads the witness through them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I thought the witness had explained the notes reflected his interview and the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The notes labeled A which are the attachment, for the record, to your 2004 witness statement, U0084018 to 4020. Whose notes are these?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Those are my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who wrote these notes into the form that you have before you?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the name at the bottom of the page or in the box stating officer's name.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who is Andreas Manthey?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Andreas was the detective who the case was turned over to at a later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you know why his name might be in that officer's name box on this page, on these pages?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I believe I do. We had a continued running log of the case, and what I believe happened, once you entered one name in there it would continuously run it even if you tried to enter it on another page. So after Andreas took over the case, he probably tried to enter his name in the following pages but was not able to so he probably maybe just forgot that by changing the one page we'll change all of them to his name, and we didn't know how to get around that. But I always referred to myself in my notes as reporting investigator, and I would put Kereakes in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And again, if you look at the last paragraph of your notes, does that remind you of what else the witness said when he picked out the suspect?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What does it say?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: That the witness positively identifies Isak Musliu as the one that beat him up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just to make this very clear for Mr. Topolski, could you please turn to tab 4 of that binder you have before you. It's the document underneath tab 4. Again, remember not to say the name. Can you tell me without the name what you see there, what this document is?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes. This is that particular witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Does your name appear on the first page of this document as the investigator taking the statement?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What is the date it says that this statement was taken?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: 17th of August, 2001. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are the notes which we looked at just a moment ago notes of this statement being taken?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you while we're here and we've talked about the notes a little bit that you took, when you took notes in the field or elsewhere, would those notes be -- how would you take those notes, handwriting, typed on a laptop? Can you describe how you would do it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Sometimes both, but if we were out in the field, I would hand write them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what would happen with those notes?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I would then come back to my office and type them up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When would you type them up again?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what does "immediately" mean? If you could be a little more specific.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: If I finished -- for example, if I finished the interview at 1600, made it back to the office by 1700 hours, I would type them up within 15 minutes, half hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then what would happen to the original notes that you had handwritten?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I would -- if it was a statement, I would then attach it to the typewritten statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What if it was not a statement?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: If there wasn't a statement, then I would throw them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And after you had obtained that signed and circled photo line-up by this witness, what did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: At this time I would attach it to that statement of the witness that I had showed it to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, I should have asked you a moment ago. This statement which you took, the same statement where the photo line-up was conducted, can you tell us how interpretation between you and the witness was conducted?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Well, it depended.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm talking about this specific --

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: This specific --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you need to, you can refer top the notes at tab 4.

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: With this particular witness, is he was able to communicate using German as a language. Then I brought in a German police officer, one of my colleagues, who did the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And were there any problems with that interpretation?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: No. We were able to get the statement documented. It had to go a little bit slow because we were transferring from German to -- then to English and it took a little bit of time, but we were able to document it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, without saying the name of the witness - you can just answer yes or no for the moment, please - did you ever visit any part of the crime scene in this case with the witness?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, private session for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, now please do not use the name, just the word "Witness." Who showed you the location of this scene which you've just described?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: The witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What did you personally observe at the site?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: There were bones protruding from the ground. Some had been scattered, but then I observed a larger area that looked like several remains could actually be seen protruding from the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In addition to you and the person you've told us brought you to this site, who else went with you, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: I had members of the missing persons unit exhumation team, members of the EOD, explosive ordnance disposal clearing team. I also had members from my detective division. An anthropologist was also brought in, an investigating judge, and -- and various other support staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you heard of the -- okay. Do you remember who came from the missing persons unit?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Yes, do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you tell us who that was?

utterances.speaker: ANARGYROS KEREAKES
utterances.text: Judy Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's actually a convenient time, Your Honour, because it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Nicholls. We will resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. We must ask you, Mr. Kereakes, to return them to carry on with your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 1st day of April, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
